title: Vitamin B6 → PLP-dependent GABA-synthesis capacity
relationship: Provides dietary B6 vitamers that pyridoxal kinase converts to PLP, the cofactor required for GAD-dependent GABA synthesis
endpoint: Established cofactor dependency; no extra-intake efficacy claim.
summary: Dietary B6 supplies precursors of the PLP cofactor required by GAD. This is a capacity relationship, not evidence that extra B6 increases brain GABA.
refs: [1] [2] [3] [4]
limits: Scope
Dietary B6 provision of PLP precursors is supported, but increasing B6 intake has not been shown to increase human brain GABA synthesis; PLP supports many enzymes and is not GABA-specific.

title: Boiled versus raw eggs → circulating essential amino acids
endpoint: Boiled eggs produced higher peak circulating essential-amino-acid concentrations than raw eggs in the tested postexercise meal, supporting PM1’s circulating precursor-provision function.
relationship: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.
summary: Boiled eggs produced higher peak circulating essential-amino-acid concentrations than raw eggs in the tested postexercise meal, supporting PM1’s circulating precursor-provision function.
input: Boiled rather than raw eggs in the tested postexercise meal
limits: Population
45 healthy resistance-trained young men; five eggs after exercise.
Endpoint
Plasma concentration is not dietary appearance flux or neuronal availability.
Separate study
Ileal digestibility was measured in five ileostomy patients, not the postexercise cohort.
Translation
No daily five-egg prescription or demonstrated muscle-protein-synthesis advantage.
confidence: Intervention confidence: not assigned — proposed rubric pending

source.input: Boiled rather than raw eggs in the tested postexercise meal

title: Tested mixed meals → acute endotoxin/LBP response
endpoint: The meal comparison measured different acute plasma endotoxin/LBP responses.
relationship: Limit gut-derived endotoxin spillover so barrier dysfunction does not drive systemic inflammatory load.
summary: The meal comparison measured different acute plasma endotoxin/LBP responses.
input: Tested fibre/fruit-rich mixed meal versus the high-fat/high-carbohydrate comparison
limits: Attribution
Multiple ingredients and macronutrients differed; no isolated fibre or fruit effect.
Measurement
LAL/LBP responses do not directly establish gut leakage, LPS bioactivity or brain benefit.
Design
Small acute parallel-group comparison; CRP and TNF-alpha did not change.

title: Post-meal walking → three-hour glucose exposure
input: Advice to walk for 10 minutes after each main meal
relationship: Postprandial glucose handling is related to the PM mission; lower exposure alone does not establish reduced glycaemic variability.
endpoint: Lower three-hour postprandial glucose incremental area under the curve versus advice to walk 30 minutes daily without specified timing.
summary: Two-week crossover periods in 41 adults with type 2 diabetes compared post-meal walking advice with untimed daily walking advice.
status: Unset — no matching admitted post-meal walking record
limits: Endpoint
Glucose exposure is not a variability endpoint.
Exposure
Advice and achieved activity differ; overall activity was greater in the post-meal condition.
Generalisability
Short study in adults with type 2 diabetes; not evidence of brain benefit.
confidence: Lifestyle confidence: provisional placement only — no rating assigned
protocol: Two-week crossover periods; 41 adults with type 2 diabetes; 10 minutes after each main meal versus 30 minutes daily without specified timing.
